segments.en: But this can be understood in light of what has been explained. For the battle of Amalek is an extremely long war. Amalek is the rod of chastisement for Israel throughout history. And the essential war is that of the evil inclination — the kelipah of Amalek — which lurks for a person always and wishes to bring him down completely. The essential subduing of it is through a firmness that is the aspect of baki b'nefik [expert in entering and exiting] — the aspect of: "If I ascend to heaven, You are there; if I make my bed in the underworld, there You are" [Tehillim 139:8] — that whatever comes upon the person throughout life, he remains strong and does not fall from anything. And this path must be learned greatly from the Tzaddikim and those joined to them — the aspect of Moshe and Yehoshua. And this is the entire work of Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur: to draw this path of teshuvah into the world.

segments.he: עִקַּר הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי הָרָצוֹן שֶׁאֵיךְ שֶׁעוֹבֵר עָלָיו בְּכָל עֵת אֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא אֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא עַל כָּל פָּנִים יְחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּרָצוֹן חָזָק מְאד לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים יִכְסֹף וְיִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא כִּי סוֹף כָּל סוֹף מַה יִּשָּׁאֵר מִמֶּנּוּ. וּבִפְרָט שֶׁכְּבָר גִּלּוּ לָנוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים אֲמִתִּיִּים שֶׁהָרָצוֹן הַטּוֹב בְּעַצְמוֹ יָקָר וְחָשׁוּב מְאד מְאד וְזֶה בְּחִינַת עִקַּר הַתַּכְלִית הָאַחֲרוֹן בְּחִינַת מָה רַב טוּבְךָ וְכוּ'. עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַזֵּק תָּמִיד בְּכָל עֵת בְּרָצוֹן חָזָק לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְעוֹרֵר וְיִתְגַּבֵּר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תָּמִיד לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בַּאֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וּתְחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת רַבּוֹת שֶׁיַּחֲמל עָלָיו ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיַמְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו הָרַחֲמָנוּת הָאֲמִתִּי שֶׁל הַמַּנְהִיג הָאֲמִתִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כִּי מְרַחֲמָם יְנַהֲגֵם. עַד שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לָצֵאת מֵהָרוּחַ שְׁטוּת וְכוּ' וּבִפְרָט לְהַרְבּוֹת בְּהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת שֶׁהִוא שִׂיחָה וּתְפִלָּה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁפּךְ לִבּוֹ כַּמַּיִם נכַח פְּנֵי ה' עַד יַשְׁקִיף וְיֵרֶא ה' מִשָּׁמַיִם וְיָאִיר עָלָיו הַדַּעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ לְבַטֵּל הָרוּחַ שְׁטוּת עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא וְיָשׁוּב מִכָּל הָעֲוֹנוֹת וְיִזְכֶּה לְהִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת. כִּי תְּפִלָּה זוֹ בְּחִינַת יִרְאָה בְּחִינַת מַה הַנַּ"ל בְּחִינַת מַ"ה ה' אֱלקֶיךָ שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה. שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה בְּחִינַת יִרְאַת ה' הִיא תִּתְהַלָּל.
segments.en: Thus in the war each person wages against his inclination, which is the war of Amalek, all victory consists of remaining firm in one's mind, in the power of the Tzaddik, holding fast and standing in the bonds of this war through all that comes upon one — for as long as one does not despair and keeps starting anew, still occupied in this war whose primary weapon is prayer, one is called a victor. For truly the battle belongs to Hashem. Now the words of the holy Zohar are understood: "Who has prevailed? The one who holds the weapon of war in his hand" — for in this war, in Israel's war from Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur, who has prevailed? Those who are still holding the weapon of war in their hands — the lulav and the four species with which they pray and complete the Hallel. For as long as Israel continues to engage in this war and hold the weapons of war in their hands, they have already prevailed — for this is the essence of victory in this war: holding fast, not despairing, and starting anew each time.

segments.he: וְכַמּוּבָא שָׁם פָּסוּק זֶה לְעִנְיַן הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן הַנַּ"ל עַיֵּן שָׁם:
segments.en: There are two aspects of prayer. There is prayer that is lower than Torah and subordinate to it; and there is prayer that is one with Torah itself, and even above it. For there is prayer in which one prays for one's physical needs — livelihood, children, life, healing, and so on. This prayer is called "temporal life," and it is below Torah and subordinate to it. For one who prays only for his bodily needs with no intention at all for the sake of Torah — such a prayer carries no weight before Hashem. It falls in the category of the "bad prayers" Rabbainu warned of — "gannava a'michdata Rachmana kari" [the thief at the moment of the break-in calls upon G-d]. It is evident to all that our days are vanity and our days like a passing shadow. When a person prays for material wealth and provision merely to fill his stomach's desires — Hashem knows that what he asks for is not truly good for him at all, since it leads him away from the purpose. Such wealth is the aspect of "riches hoarded by their owner to his harm." Thus prayer purely for bodily needs without the intention of fulfilling Torah is certainly of no value whatsoever. The Zohar criticizes such prayers: "They bark like dogs: give us life, give us food..." Yet when one prays for bodily needs for the sake of Torah fulfillment — that is, one prays for children, life, and livelihood with the entire intent of being able to fulfill Hashem's will and keep His Torah — then Hashem does take pleasure in such prayer. But even so, this prayer is below Torah and subordinate to it, for since the prayer is for bodily needs, the prayer itself without the Torah has no standing. Why does one need the body and its needs? Today here, tomorrow in the grave. Such prayer has no life or substance except through Torah — through the intention of keeping Torah. Therefore it is indeed subordinate to Torah. Such prayer must be guarded greatly lest the outer forces take hold of it and it become the aspect of "her feet descend to death." One must be expert in this subtle point lest the Sitra Achra twist one's intention from its Torah-directed focus toward bodily ends purely for the body's sake — at which point the prayer becomes disqualified.

But the essential complete prayer is when one prays solely for the needs of one's own soul — that is, all of one's prayers are to merit awe of Hashem and serving Him. As King Dovid said: "One thing have I asked of Hashem; that shall I seek: to dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life" [Tehillim 27:4]. Such prayer is not subordinate to Torah — on the contrary, it is the very fulfillment of Torah. For one is asking only to fulfill Torah, which is the essence of its completeness: "It is not the study that is primary but the deed." This is the meaning of: "A woman who fears Hashem shall be praised" [Mishlei 31:30] — the prayer that is in the aspect of the Woman of Valor [aishes chayil], when directed toward awe of Hashem, toward meriting that awe — she shall be praised. For that is the ultimate completeness of prayer. And this prayer is equivalent to Torah and even above it. Because the essential intention in Torah study is to fulfill the Torah — "not study but deed" — and this is exactly the intent of such prayer, to merit fulfilling the Torah. Therefore Torah and prayer are equal in stature, and prayer is even higher. For this prayer is the aspect of "a woman who fears Hashem" — the aspect of: "The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem" [Tehillim 111:10] — namely, it is above wisdom, which is Torah, because prayer for the sake of yiras Shomayim [awe of Heaven] is the very fulfillment of Torah. For "all is in the hands of Heaven except awe of Heaven." And through prayer one can attain awe of Heaven — this is the aspect of the entire Book of Tehillim, which King Dovid composed, entirely as prayers to merit awe of Heaven and service of Hashem.
